subject.title: fix(agents): prevent Windows shell startup bypassing auto-review

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally restrict automatic review for Windows `cmd` to explicit `/d /c` invocations with only the documented non-binding startup options before the command payload?
rationale: This is an intentional security/compatibility boundary: a stricter parser protects against unreviewed startup behavior but may route uncommon existing Windows command forms to human approval.

options.title: Adopt the fail-closed boundary
options.body: Merge after validating the documented switch allowlist and exact-head caller coverage, accepting human approval for ambiguous `cmd` startup forms.

options.title: Preserve broader auto-review compatibility
options.body: Keep a broader supported `cmd` grammar only if maintainers can define and test how every additional form remains transparent to review.

recommendation.title: Adopt the fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Merge after validating the documented switch allowlist and exact-head caller coverage, accepting human approval for ambiguous `cmd` startup forms.
